label: CONTAINED_IN_1, generic: an intrinsic determination of the bearer, intentional or virtual
term: contained in a bearer (Contains b e)
definition: Contains b e: the item e is contained in the bearer b, as an intrinsic determination or as the bearer's own nature, not as a separate being. Containment may be intentional (an idea, the form of another as other) or virtual (a power to produce, a mode in which the bearer's nature is imitable); this generic sense CONTAINED_IN_1 does not say which (the intentional sense CONTAINED_IN_2 is DEF c82c75e9-1786-43f1-8e0d-1b295ae5699a, the virtual sense CONTAINED_IN_3 DEF 1294c8f3-3eb6-4960-859e-506ccdee6ab8). Examples: an idea in a mind; a disposition of a body; the one nature of a simple source. Non-examples: an abstract object that exists whether or not the bearer does; a product the bearer has made outside itself. Structural properties: a declared primitive two-place relation; it implies neither apprehension nor production.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 premise lane C), attribution deferred. See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Individuating non-present candidates: the axiarchic rival and the cognition criterion'. Lean: the generic sense is the parameter Contains : B → C → Prop, named by ContainsGenerically. The q.4 a.2 notion of formal and virtual containment of a perfection in a cause (DEF d7e7ae08-0ebe-519d-ba9d-e349998103dc) is related but distinct: it concerns perfections of effects in their causes, not stand-ins of candidates in a favouring. That intentional and virtual containment are not separated by the generic relation is deliberate: the containment-recognition bridge is exactly the step between them.
